init.title: DWD Precipitation options
init.description: These settings change how the sensors present DWD's data. None of them affect how often it is fetched — each product is refreshed as soon as DWD publishes it, and failed fetches are retried automatically.

data.extra_state_attributes: Add technical details to each sensor
data.precipitation_reset_threshold: Rain needed to reset the dry-streak counter (mm)
data.dry_streak_source: Product that resets the dry-streak counter

data_description.extra_state_attributes: Attaches the DWD product name, the measurement time and the period each value covers to every sensor as attributes. Useful in templates or when reporting a problem; leave it off otherwise.
data_description.precipitation_threshold: How much forecast rain counts as precipitation for the “Precipitation start”, “Precipitation end” and “Precipitation expected” sensors. 0 means any amount DWD detects; raise it to around 0.5 to ignore drizzle.
data_description.start_end_mode: Whether those two sensors show a clock time (“14:25”) or the minutes until the event (“20”). Whichever you do not pick stays available as an attribute on the same sensor.
data_description.precipitation_reset_threshold: How much rain resets “Timespan without precipitation” to zero. It is compared against the past-hour total of the selected product, in millimetres accumulated over that hour — so 1 mm means 1 mm fell within the hour, not a rate.
data_description.dry_streak_source: Which past-hour total “Timespan without precipitation” compares against the reset threshold. “Gauge-adjusted hour” (RW) is corrected with rain-gauge data and more accurate: DWD's analysis of the latest 60 minutes, rerun every 10 minutes, so a reset shows about 30 to 40 minutes after the rain. “Precipitation last 60 min” (RS) is radar only and updated every 5 minutes: faster, but noisier, and its rolling hour keeps resetting the counter for up to an hour after the rain stops.

advanced_options.name: Advanced options
advanced_options.description: Settings most installations never need to change.

data.precipitation_end_algorithm: When “Precipitation end” counts rain as over
data.full_rolling_series: Include the past hour in the hourly forecast series
data.unavailable_when_stale: Show sensors as unavailable when the data is out of date

data_description.rain_events: Adds the “Rain events” sensor, which follows each burst of rain from the first forecast that shows it until it has fallen, for blueprints that warn about or report rain. Off by default. When it is on, or the location has a rain warning, the integration also fetches the radar analyses it missed and keeps a small record of recent rain on disk.
data_description.rain_event_threshold: How much rain a 5-minute step needs to count towards a rain event, for the “Rain events” sensor and the rain warnings. 0 means any trace forms an event. Independent of the rain detection threshold, so the events and “Precipitation start” can disagree when the two differ.
data_description.precipitation_end_algorithm: “First dry gap” reports the end of the current burst, so it moves around during showers. “Precipitation clears within 2 h” waits until no further rain is forecast, which is steadier but stays unknown longer. DWD forecasts only two hours ahead, so beyond that the sensor is “unknown” either way.
data_description.full_rolling_series: Makes the “forecast_rolling_1h” attribute of “Peak hourly precipitation next 120 min” start one hour earlier. Each entry is the rain in the hour starting at that time, so the first entries also include rain that has already fallen, and a chart shows the past hour and the forecast as one curve. The sensor's value is the same either way, as it only looks at the hours ahead. The earlier hour is built from the radar analyses of the past hour, without any extra download, so after a restart it appears once the integration has run for an hour.
data_description.unavailable_when_stale: If DWD does not publish a new file in time, the affected sensors report “unavailable” instead of keeping the last value. Turn this off to always keep the most recent reading, accepting that it may be hours old. Either way the missing file keeps being retried in the background.

user.title: Add a rain warning
user.description: A rain warning turns on shortly before rain reaches this location, and stays on while it rains. Each warning is a device of its own, named after the location and the warning (“Home Laundry”), with two entities: “Rain warning” (on/off) and “Rain warning status” (dry, soon or rain, with the details of the rain event). It works on the rain events the integration tracks, so the advanced option “Rain event threshold” decides what counts as rain.

data.name: Name
data.min_peak_1h: Minimum rain in the wettest hour (mm)
data.min_peak_10min: Minimum rain in the wettest 10 minutes (mm)

data_description.name: What the warning is for, such as “Laundry” or “Windows”. At a location named “Home”, “Laundry” gives the device “Home Laundry” and binary_sensor.home_laundry_rain_warning.
data_description.lead_time: How many minutes before the rain the warning turns on. The forecast reaches two hours ahead and arrives a few minutes after DWD's release, so the warning can come up to 5 minutes later than this.
data_description.min_mm: Only warn about a rain event that brings at least this much in total, measured and forecast. Leave empty to warn about every rain event.
data_description.min_peak_1h: Only warn about a rain event whose wettest hour brings at least this much. Leave empty to ignore it.
data_description.min_peak_10min: Only warn about a rain event whose wettest 10 minutes bring at least this much, for short heavy bursts. Leave empty to ignore it.
data_description.combine: Whether an event has to reach one of the minimums you set, or all of them. Without a minimum it does not matter.

reconfigure.title: Change the rain warning
reconfigure.description: A new name renames the warning's device and entities; their entity ids stay as they are.
